s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with electrocardiographic changes and elevated cardiac biomarkers
salient_findings: Sudden-onset chest pain
Tachycardia with a pulse of 120 beats/min
Elevated high-sensitivity troponin I and brain-type natriuretic peptide
ECG findings of ST-segment elevation and PR-segment depression
Normal coronary arteries on coronary angiography
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 60s
History of hypertension
No history of acute febrile illness
No family history of sudden cardiac death
Normal blood pressure
Elevated white blood cell count
Normal serum calcium
High-sensitivity troponin I: 1.15 ng/mL
Brain-type natriuretic peptide: 1060.30 pg/mL
ECG showed sinus tachycardia and PR-segment elevation in lead aVR
ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, aVF, and V2 to V6
Systolic apical ballooning on left ventriculography
Left-adrenal heterogeneous mass on contrast-enhanced abdominal CT

Elevated white blood cell count
Normal serum calcium
High-sensitivity troponin I: 1.15 ng/mL

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with sudden-onset chest pain, elevated troponin, and brain-type natriuretic peptide, along with the ECG findings and the presence of systolic apical ballooning on left ventriculography, are characteristic of takotsubo cardiomyopathy. The absence of coronary artery disease on angiography further supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: myocardial infarction
rejected.why: Normal coronary arteries on angiography make this less likely

rejected.label: acute myocardial infarction
rejected.why: Normal coronary arteries and the pattern of apical ballooning are not typical for acute myocardial infarction

rejected.label: heart failure
rejected.why: While the patient has elevated brain-type natriuretic peptide, the primary issue appears to be an acute cardiac event rather than chronic heart failure

rejected.label: cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: This is a broader category, and takotsubo cardiomyopathy is a more specific diagnosis that fits the patient's presentation
